input.quote: IBM reserves the right to investigate potential violations of the representations and warranties in Subsection 11.2(b).
input.rationale: The only Customer-binding verification right in the Agreement is IBM's reserved right in 11.3 to investigate potential violations of Customer's AUP warranty; there is no audit/inspection clause elsewhere (no responsive language in 5.3, 11.5, 13.2 or the general terms). That right is unlimited in frequency, requires no advance notice (the notice attempt in the following paragraph applies only before IBM restricts access or removes Content, and is excused in an emergency), and allocates no cost, which is walk-away territory under this rule. We therefore propose the shortest fallback cure: one investigation per year, 15 days' notice, and IBM bearing cost unless an underpayment exceeding 10% is found. We have not pursued the preferred parameters (30 days, independent auditor, off-site, 5%, no system access) as the fallback is an acceptable landing zone.

ops.text: IBM may investigate potential violations under this Subsection 11.3 no more than once per year, and only after giving Customer at least fifteen (15) days' notice. IBM will bear all costs of any such investigation unless it reveals an underpayment by Customer exceeding ten percent (10%).

proposal.comment: [Playbook] IBM's right to investigate our use of the Services under 11.3 is currently unlimited, unannounced and at our potential cost. We have added our fallback audit parameters - once per year, 15 days' notice, and IBM bearing the cost unless an underpayment exceeding 10% is found.
proposal.summary: Add frequency, notice and cost limits to IBM's investigation right in 11.3

mappings.element: Vendor may audit no more than once per year.
Vendor must give at least 15 days' notice of an audit.
Vendor bears audit costs unless underpayment exceeds 10 percent.
